record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.context_brief: Muon EDM and new CP violation
record.original_question: Search for CP violation beyond the CKM mechanism through electric dipole moments, especially the muon electric dipole moment. Since Standard Model CKM predictions for EDMs are far below experimental goals, the open question is whether new sources of CP violation can produce a measurable EDM, potentially at sensitivities comparable to existing constraints on the anomalous magnetic moment.

evidence.quote: If all CP-violation is encoded in the CKM matrix, EDMs are too small to measure. Therefore EDMs are an excellent place to look for CP-violation beyond the Standard Model.
Attempts to explain the origin of the baryon excess in the Universe suggest that other sources of CP-violation may be waiting to be discovered.
So EDM measurements at a sensitivity comparable to existing limits on aµ could provide fertile ground in which to look for new sources of CP-violation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model, all CP violation in the quark sector is encoded in the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa (CKM) mixing matrix. As a consequence, the CKM-induced contribution to the electric dipole moment (EDM) of a charged lepton, defined through the interaction Lagrangian L = -(d_ℓ/2) ψ̄ σ^{μν} iγ_5 ψ F_{μν}, is many orders of magnitude below current and projected experimental sensitivities. However, the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe requires additional sources of CP violation beyond the CKM mechanism.

Question: Determine whether new (beyond–Standard-Model) sources of CP violation can produce a nonzero muon electric dipole moment d_μ that is measurable at a sensitivity comparable to existing constraints on the muon anomalous magnetic moment a_μ = (g_μ − 2)/2. Specifically, identify viable theoretical frameworks beyond the Standard Model in which |d_μ| is large enough to be observed by foreseeable experiments (e.g., at the level of 10^{-21}–10^{-24} e·cm), and decide experimentally whether such a nonzero muon EDM exists.
artifact.category_tag: Muon electric dipole moment and CP violation
artifact.status_search_result: No nonzero muon EDM has been measured. Current and proposed experiments (e.g., the dedicated muon EDM search at PSI using a frozen-spin technique, with Phase I target sensitivity ~4×10^{-21} e·cm and Phase II ~6×10^{-23} e·cm, and a search at the Fermilab Muon g-2 experiment) aim to improve sensitivity by several orders of magnitude. Recent theoretical work (2022–2026) continues to analyze the muon EDM as a probe of flavor-diagonal CP violation within SMEFT and various UV completions, indicating the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: A compact frozen-spin trap for the search for the electric dipole moment of the muon
status_evidence.snippet: Phase I expected sensitivity 4×10^{-21} e·cm; Phase II target 6×10^{-23} e·cm.
status_evidence.claim: A dedicated muon EDM search is being built at PSI; no measurement yet, indicating the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Muon Electric Dipole Moment as a Probe of Flavor-Diagonal CP Violation
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies SMEFT operators to which muon EDM is most sensitive and UV completions producing observable d_μ.
status_evidence.claim: Active theoretical investigation into BSM sources of CP violation generating measurable d_μ.

status_evidence.title: Chasing the muon EDM to constrain the SMEFT and UV models
status_evidence.snippet: Examines vector-like leptons, heavy vector bosons, and two Higgs doublet models.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2026) work confirms the muon EDM remains an open probe of BSM CP violation.

status_evidence.title: Search for a Permanent Muon Electric Dipole Moment at the Fermilab Muon g-2 Experiment
status_evidence.snippet: Search ongoing at Fermilab Muon g-2.
